title: Show a friendly message when no invoices match
body:
When the table would be empty (for example a status filter with no matches), show "No invoices match this filter" instead of an empty table.

---
_Generated by [Claude Code](https://claude.ai/code)_

spec.plan:
Before: app/invoices/page.tsx renders its unconditionally, so a list with no rows would render a header row over an empty body. After: the table markup moves verbatim into a new server component app/invoices/InvoiceTable.tsx taking `invoices: readonly Invoice[]`, which renders `

No invoices match this filter

` when that list is empty and the existing table otherwise; the page passes listInvoices() straight through, so with the seeded data every pixel stays the same. Scope. This app has no status filter: listInvoices() returns a hard-coded five-invoice array (lib/invoices.ts:11), so the empty state is not reachable through the UI today — the request names a filter only as an example of when the table would be empty. Adding a filter is a separate work item and is NOT part of this one — it is already filed as issue #27, "Filter the invoices table by status". The empty state is therefore checked two ways: in the running app by temporarily emptying the seed (acceptance check 2, a scratch edit that must be reverted and never committed), and by the new unit test. Why a component rather than a conditional inside the page. app/invoices/page.test.tsx already renders the page, so the page is at 100% line coverage, but it can only ever produce the seeded non-empty list — testing the empty branch in place would need vi.mock of @/lib/invoices, a pattern this repo does not use and one the shared rubric treats as a weak test. A component that takes the list as a prop is testable both ways with the render/plain-DOM pattern already in components/ExportButton.test.tsx. It goes beside the page, not in components/, because the feature map reserves components/ for UI a page and something else both need, or for UI needing browser APIs — this is neither. Builder details, so nothing is left to decide: 1. New app/invoices/InvoiceTable.tsx. No "use client" — it is a server component. One import: `import { formatAmount, type Invoice } from "@/lib/invoices";` (@/ form, because it crosses a folder). Export `function InvoiceTable({ invoices }: { invoices: readonly Invoice[] })`. First an early return for `invoices.length === 0` with the paragraph above — marginTop 1.5rem so the spacing matches the table it replaces. Then the existing
block copied verbatim from page.tsx lines 13-32: same inline styles, same four columns (Invoice, Customer, Amount, Status), same `key={i.id}`, same `formatAmount(i.amountCents)`. 2. app/invoices/page.tsx: add `import { InvoiceTable } from "./InvoiceTable";` — extensionless, NOT "./InvoiceTable.js", which type-checks and passes vitest but fails `next build` with "Module not found". Replace the whole
…
block with ``. Drop `formatAmount` from the @/lib/invoices import, which is now unused and is an eslint error. Leave the

, the and the "Total sent" paragraph exactly as they are. 3. New app/invoices/InvoiceTable.test.tsx: `import { InvoiceTable } from "./InvoiceTable.js";` (the .js form is right in a test file and resolves under vitest), `afterEach(cleanup)`, and the `invoice(over: Partial = {})` factory in the style of lib/invoices.test.ts:7 rather than literal objects. Two cases, named for what a reader loses if they fail. Plain DOM assertions, no jest-dom. 4. Do not modify app/invoices/page.test.tsx: the DOM it asserts on is unchanged, so its two tests still pass as written. No new dependency, no new markdown file, nothing changed under lib/ or components/.
acceptance_checks: With the repo's seeded data untouched, build and start the app (`npm run build`, `npm run start -- --port 3000`) and open http://localhost:3000/invoices: the table still lists all five invoices INV-1001 to INV-1005 with their Invoice/Customer/Amount/Status columns, the button still reads "Export 3 invoices as CSV", the page still reads "Total sent: $1,497.50", and the text "No invoices match this filter" does not appear anywhere on the page.

Temporarily empty the seed to reach the state the request is about: edit lib/invoices.ts so INVOICES is `[]`, rebuild and restart, then open http://localhost:3000/invoices — the page shows the text "No invoices match this filter" and no <table> element at all (not a header row over an empty body). Then restore the seed with `git checkout -- lib/invoices.ts`, rebuild, and confirm the page is back to five rows. This scratch edit must not be committed.

Run `npm test`: the new app/invoices/InvoiceTable.test.tsx case that renders <InvoiceTable invoices={[]} /> passes, asserting the rendered output contains exactly the text "No invoices match this filter" and that querying for a table element returns null.

Run `npm test`: the new app/invoices/InvoiceTable.test.tsx case that renders <InvoiceTable /> with two invoices passes, asserting three rows are present (the header row plus one per invoice), that both invoice ids appear, and that "No invoices match this filter" does not appear — so the extraction did not change the table a user sees.

Run `npm test -- --coverage`, `npm run typecheck` and `npm run lint`: all three exit 0, the whole existing suite still passes including app/invoices/page.test.tsx unmodified, and the coverage table shows app/invoices/InvoiceTable.tsx and app/invoices/page.tsx at 100% of lines, which keeps diff coverage above the 80% minimum in .factory/guardrails/coverage.json.

research.claim: There is no status filter anywhere in the app: the page renders every invoice listInvoices() returns, and that is a hard-coded readonly array of five invoices. So the empty table the request describes cannot be produced through the UI today, and the request's "status filter" is an example, not a thing to build.
research.source: app/invoices/page.tsx:5 — `const invoices = listInvoices();` feeds the table directly; lib/invoices.ts:11-17 is the hard-coded INVOICES array

research.claim: The table markup that must move is page.tsx lines 13-32: a <table> with marginTop 1.5rem and borderCollapse collapse, four columns, and one <tr key={i.id}> per invoice. Copying it verbatim keeps the rendered DOM identical, which is why app/invoices/page.test.tsx needs no edit.

A new line that no test executes therefore costs real coverage, which is why the empty-state branch must be exercised by a test rather than only read.

research.claim: Importing a sibling source module as "./InvoiceTable.js" breaks the production build, even though tsc and vitest both accept it. Next's webpack resolver does not rewrite .js to .tsx for app source. Extensionless "./InvoiceTable" builds, type-checks and lints clean. The .js form stays correct in test files, which never go through next build.

Probe deleted, tree left clean.

research.claim: An unused import is a hard error here, so page.tsx must drop formatAmount when the table leaves it. typescript-eslint's recommended set is enabled and reports @typescript-eslint/no-unused-vars as an error.

research.claim: A feature-local component belongs beside the page, not in components/: that folder is for UI a page and something else both need, or UI needing browser APIs a server component cannot have, and the map is explicit that one caller is not a shared concern.

The component test pattern to follow: render with @testing-library/react, afterEach(cleanup), plain DOM property assertions instead of jest-dom (a deliberate choice to keep the dependency list short), and an invoice(over) factory for data rather than literal objects.
research.source: components/ExportButton.test.tsx:5 and :25-27 (the comment stating the jest-dom choice); lib/invoices.test.ts:7-10 (the factory)

research.claim: Styling must be an inline style={{}} object — there is no CSS file, class name or styling library in the repo — and the existing table carries marginTop 1.5rem, so the empty-state paragraph carries the same to keep the spacing under the export button unchanged.

The sandbox can verify both browser checks: it builds and runs the production server, /invoices is server-rendered so a screenshot shows the real table, and a rebuild after a scratch edit to lib/invoices.ts is within the same install/build/run loop the trial already exercises.
